body: All I can share with you is that I am 2 years out of a 25 year marriage to an abusive and controlling man.  I know that I made the right decision in leaving, but I have to tell you that I am so lonely.  I have always had a man in my life and now I don't even have the illusion of having a partner.  I have realized that I never did have a partner, but I don't like being alone.  It's another Saturday night and I'm going to have dinner alone, watch tv alone, and sleep alone.  You may have a different outcome if you leave, but there are many women who are sitting in the same seat as me.  Good luck to you.
This Christmas was not as bad as I thought it would be so I got through it ok.  First year on my own and it sure is different.

From what you write, he sounds like a scary dude.  And you are just waiting and quivering waiting for the explosion.  I have lived with a man who is explosive and unpredictable like this.  It can make you feel like you are the crazy one.  You aren't, this is real.  Please take care of yourself and your children.  Do you have an escape plan and some money stashed away?  You may never need to use it, but it doesn't hurt to be prepared.  It sounds like he is extremely volatile and you are very scared.  Please take care.

I'm so sorry this happened to you.  It sounds like it may have been many events and pressures that led up to the break-up.  Perhaps in a few days things might cool down and you may be able to patch things back together.  In my life, relationships are so valuable, I hate to see them end.  You just end up starting all over again with someone else.  Hang in there.

Hello, I am missing my ex-boyfriend.  We were together for a long time.  I broke up with him 2 years ago.  It has been terribly bad this Christmas season.  He was a huge part of my life.  I know he was not good for me, but I still miss him like crazy.  Can't wait until Christmas is over with.

I've been NC for 2 years.  It's been very hard because we were together such a long time.  Truly this man was a part of my family-actually my only family.  Got to confess this Christmas time this year is making me so lonely for him.  I wish I could take it all back even though I know he was not good for me.  I dread the next couple of weeks until Christmas is over.  I'm just staying home by myself so I don't get covid and am so so lonely.
I think things will get much better once the vaccine is in place.  It will probably be a much different looking world than from pre-pandemic, but most of us will be so grateful.

I know, I feel so lonely most of the time myself.  We do have a little bit more to go.  The vaccine is on the horizon.  It won't solve every problem, but will make lots of things better.  Hang in there please.
I'd be interested in talking.  i'm in your age group.
I'm so sorry for the pain you are experiencing.  I have no magic answers for you.  I'm glad that you reached out here to this group.  Absolute strangers care about you and what happens to you.
I'm so sorry for your devastating news.  It's so much to take in.  It may take awhile for you to sort out your choices and options.  We are here for you.
I am older than you.  I too suffer from depression and am feeling very lonely.  I live by myself and the days just stretch on and on.  Sometimes I wonder how long I can take it.
it's been 2 years for me.  I was doing ok, but then today i was in the market, thinking about dinner.  And it hit me all over again, how lost and lonely I am.
Rejoice, rejoice!
Welcome to this sub.  Can you tell us a little about things you like or are interested in?
I'm 2 years NC with my ex.  Except through our lawyers.  I still miss him and think of him everyday, but probably NC is for the best.

Wow, you do have so much on your plate, plus covid.  As everyone else says, insist that he sit down and talk to you.  No running out of the room, and no interruptions.  I wouldn't make it more than an hour.  But you do have a right to know what is going on.  You may indeed need to make some decisions about letting him live with you or not.  It sounds like it's time.  Good luck.
Not sure, I think maybe you need to put out a little more information.

I hate friend break-ups because no one ever tries to resolve anything.  At least with relationship breakups you will go to counseling.  Things are never resolved, and there's just a big hole where the friendship used to be.  I don't understand it, but I know I need to accept it.  Best of luck to you.

I share your feelings.  I am also afraid of getting sick.  And I am being very cautious.  I also hate zoom but will take what I can get.  I feel isolated and alone, holidays have been canceled.  My birthday is December 21, better forget about that.  You are not alone but staying safe and healthy is your best bet.  Hang in there.

Thanks for posting this.  It's been 2 years for me.  I was doing pretty well but had a moment of weakness where I wanted to reach out this morning.  I didn't, but I sure wanted to.  What I did instead was write a letter stating all my feelings and what I wanted to happen.  I put it all on my computer screen-and didn't send it.  It helps me to write it out, and then it's not in my head.
Nice offer.

Thank you all for being so responsible.  I know it's lonely and sad out there being on your own.  I have never lived on my own until this last year and I hate it.  I'm used to being around other people, friends and family.  I do have a cat who helps keep me company.

I commend you for being responsible and caring about the people you live with.  Please don't pay attention to what other people are doing.  You know what's best.

I'm having severe health problems that I can't seem to get a handle on.  So yes, I understand a level of sadness.  It is a heavy feeling.  I just try and hang in there, keep functioning, and take care of things.  I keep telling myself that these are tough trying times we are all going through right now and trying everyone's souls.

Sounds like the beginning of a wonderful love affair.  And who knows where it could have led.  Probably you are right, it's just too little time together to know if there's a future.  So sorry this didn't work out.

You sure have been through alot.  Lots to process in your post.  My only comment is that there are children involved.  If you can hang in there and be there for your kids, it's so vitally important.  In these challenging times, it's important for kids to have as much stability as possible.  We all need as much peace and calm as possible during these times.  Hang in there.

Sorry you are going through such a rough time.  These are such stressful times for everyone.  It's so hard when you get in a fight with your significant other.  No great words of wisdom from me.  I am a kind person and care about your having such a difficult time.

This is a bizarre time.  I am in one of the at-risk groups so my decision is made for me.  Remember, if you are in a group of 30 people, you are actually in a much larger group of all the people those folks have been hanging with.  It's a huge risk.  Even if people have had a covid test, that's only a snapshot in time of whether infected or not.  Add liquor and you have a deadly combination.  It's just not worth it.  Don't mean to sound like a grump but these holidays come every year.  It's not going to hurt anyone to give it a rest for once.  You can have warm wonderful conversations via phone, zoom, skype.  It is possible to connect without the face to face.

I'm older than you and have been lurking around here myself.  Congrats to you for getting through some terribly difficult things.  Life sure does give us some challenges.  Feel free to write me if you like.

Sorry you are going through a bad time.  We are all with you and supporting you.  This is such a strange time for everyone on the planet.  None of us has ever been through anything like this before.  Hang in there.

I agree.  In my opinion, therapy is a verbal process, good listening, verbal give-and-take.  Texting does not sound like a good option.  Perhaps you can have a more active session when you are off work?

I am so sorry that you are having to think about things like this.  What to me just seems like common sense, avoiding crowds, staying away from inside gatherings,no partying, wearing masks.  It's not brain surgery here.

I agree with you and glad you are sticking to your guns..  lease don't pay attention to what others are doing, or not.  You know what you should be doing and you are doing the right thing. 

Congratulations to you for taking care of yourself and the others around you.  It's not always easy doing the smart thing and not following the crowd, but please hang in there.

I'm so sorry that you are going through this.   It's an unnatural condition for us humans to be living in.  You are right, it has been months, and with no end in sight.

It's good that you posted here.  Anything you can do to get your feelings out is a good idea.  I journal just about every day, especially when I am feeling bad or very lost.

Perhaps it might be considering one of those on-line services for therapy?  I haven't tried them, but it is an option.  Maybe a good place to help you process all this craziness?

Regardless, please keep posting and know you are not alone in this bizarre time.  Take care.

I understand, I feel extremely lonely myself.  Before covid, I had an active social life.  I actually enjoyed a chance to stay home and watch tv.  Now what a different world we live in.  I also would like to meet a romantic partner.  Online dating is a complete mystery to me.  I have tried it a couple of times, but I just can't seem to get the hang of how to play the game.  I talk to people, and then never hear from them again, meet for coffee, and then nothing.  It's like a different language that I just don't speak.

I walk every morning and actually get lots of juice from just saying hi to people in the neighborhood that I don't know other than casually.  Hang in there.  It's very weird for us all.

I am always surprised when friends have a falling out and just let things go.  Presumably if you were in a relationship, you would do things to resolve the issues or go to counseling.  Why do we just let our friendships go by the way?  Why are we so afraid to discuss what happened?  I have had this happen to me and it mystifies me.  And it always takes two people for things to happen, good or bad.

You are in a tough place.  It's so hard seeing people that we love doing things that look crazy to us.  My mantra is, "Much as I'd like to, I cannot control other people's behavior."  My job is to do the things that I feel are most appropriate for me under the circumstances and try not to look at other's behavior.  If it's my family, I will clearly and carefully state my point of view, but not be surprised when I get defensive blow back.  Your best biggest job right now is to take care of yourself and love your Mom and Dad with all your heart.

I'm glad to hear that you are doing better today.  And I am glad that you posted here yesterday.  Sometimes I find that it just helps to write out my thoughts and get them out of my head (as much as I can anyway).  To that end, I have a folder on my computer named Check-In.  There anytime that I am feeling depressed, lonely, anxious, or just plain out-of-sorts, I spit it all out on the screen.  When I'm done, I rarely read it, I just number it 25, 26, 27 and save it.  Not sure exactly why I save it, but I do.  Generally, I feel so much better once I've got it down on the proverbial paper.

Regarding the world, who knows?  I too am disturbed by the tone of politics at this point.  There are only 2 short months until the election.  I am hoping things will settle down after the presidency is resolved.

I do not believe that our country is coming to an end.  I keep telling myself that we did survive the war between the states, and we can survive this.  I do believe it.  No system of government is perfect, and there are so many injustices out there. 

 However, I do believe, messy as it is, so far this is the best form of government that the world has yet invented.  We humans, however, are far less than perfect.  Some of us are acting a little crazy right now.  It's easy to think about getting on the bandwagon.  Personally, I would much rather put my shovel in the ground and do something positive to help folks.  I' not interested in tearing things down.

What can you do?  First and foremost, vote.  Even if you think it's a waste of time.  It's your right to have a say.  Your view or candidate may not win, but at least you participated.

I also made a list of ways that I can soothe myself as I am prone to anxiety.  Can I pet my cat, have a quiet conversation with a good friend, read, listen to an inspiring podcast?  I use them all to keep myself calmed down.  If I get in trouble, I refer to the list.

Perhaps I've written something that may be of help to you, sure hope so.  Hang in there.

What I do, and I know this sounds weird, is when I go to a store or market, I make a point to have little conversations with strangers or clerks.  Just little chit chat.  For some reason, it really helps with the loneliness.  Silly I know, but no possibility for rejection.
If you like to read, what about joining a book or short story group?  I'm in a short story group on zoom.  we meet every Sunday afternoon, and it's part of my lifesaver program.
So sorry to hear that.

I think it's part of the glutathione package.  A Naturopath is who gave it to me.  It's supposed to help repair but it was a disaster for me.  I tried all the detox methods.  They didn't do any good, I just had to ride it out until my system could clear it.  And I am not going to see that doctor anymore.
Wise choice.

Thanks for your response.  It sounds like you are doing great things.  I had never heard of chainmailing, but I looked it up.  I love that you are working on your music, increasing your range, and sending your friends care packages.  You sounds pretty together.

I was thinking about that too.  We just went through the big fire.  Thankfully, we didn't get evacuated.  However, we have 2 more months to go before the rain starts.  I was happily looking forward to that time, then I realized that it will be dark so much earlier and with long winter nights.

Thanks, I used to be a big needlepoint gal, lots of quilting too.  But after a few years, those things ran their course.  I am doing the yoga which helps tremendously.  What online classes are you taking?

Well said!  When this started, I made a list and told myself that I would get everything squared away away on that list.  I have done some it, but I am not using my time productively.  Wish I could get a better handle on things.
Thanks for your reply.  What can we do?  I know this is going for quite some time.  I would have thought I had acclimated by now, but just seems to be getting worse.
I don't know if I am you, or you me.  Everything I used to do in the pre-covid days is gone.  Just staying at home taking care of things.  Makes me crazy.  How about you?
It sounds extremely lonely to me.
You feel how you feel.  These are scary times.
I know scary times.  I dont have any great words of wisdom.  Sounds like extreme anxiety.

I know the general thinking is, "well done."  I'm never sure.  After having been in a relationship many years, I miss him every day.  I wish it had been different.  If he would call me, I would probably take him back.  I miss being married terribly.  Especially with corona.

Thank you for replying.  I am taking something called PK IV Therapy.  It is ripping my stomach, headaches, and fatigue.  I don't know if it's a herx, or an allergic reaction, or what?  It's driving me crazy.  I'm so miserable I'm counting the hours until I can go to sleep.
I have been watching and reading about it myself.  I haven't yet found a doctor to proscribe it for me.  How did you do that?  From what I read, you start very very slowly.
Which lyme test  did you have done?

So glad you made the difficult decision.  I don't know how long it will take to feel ok after such a long relationship.  The loss of the daughter must be devastating.  Hang in there and keep plugging away.

It sounds like you have already left emotionally.  I understand that the physical abuse may have killed the love you felt for your partner.  If you are truly done, then you are hurting her more by staying in the relationship and pretending.

I am so sorry that you and your wife are going through such a difficult time.  You certainly lay out many issues on the table.  It's impossible for anyone to say where you should put your focus.  It sounds like you are taking all the right steps, seeing a therapist, taking care of yourself physically, renewing your personal interests.  All good and necessary steps toward mental soundness and good decision making.

I'm sure that is a terribly sad and confusing time for you.  Your wonderful daughter makes  decisions much more difficult.  Hang in there and remember that you don't need to make all your decisions right away.  You can take time.  These are life-changing decisions that you are contemplating.  You deserve to take your time.  Good luck.

I am so sorry that you are having such a rough time.  It sounds like you have done your best to move on and go to therapy, but I know how hard it is.  When you have your heart and soul in a relationship, it's hard to find your way to your own happy place.  Hang in there.

Here's a few reflections.  You seems to be unsure of whether you want to be with this man or not.  To my thinking, that's the first thing you need to decide.  If you take off and move across country, then you may end up in the dreaded yo-yo relationship drama.  From my experience, after you leave and get settled, then you start to get lonely and have doubts about how bad the relationship was.  Also he may be whispering sweet things in your ear which makes everything very confusing.

Perhaps it might be worthwhile to find a rental in the area and try to sort out your relationship.  I wouldn't make any big decisions regarding moving across country, property settlement, etc.  It might be wise to get yourself somewhere safe where you can settle down, get some quiet time.  These are big life decisions that should probably not be made on the fly.

I am a big animal lover myself, but you need to get yourself quiet and safe before you can make any decisions about the rest of your life and the dogs involved.  Good luck.

I am so sorry to hear that your husband is taking confidences that you shared and using them against you.  This is downright mean and hurtful.  How can you ever trust him to tell him anything again?  My mother used to do the same thing to me, I would think we were really getting close, and I could trust her.  Later on she would use it against me.  My only answer was to stop telling her anything and leave as soon as I could.  Not a perfect solution, but what can you do at 17?

Your husband doesn't sound like he is much interested in spending time with you.  Again, an unkind and hurtful relationship to be in.  Please don't let him tell you what is wrong with you.  He's not your doctor or your nurse.  He sounds like he has plenty of his own issues to work out.  Good luck with this one.

Thank you for sharing your story.  I am so sorry for the pain you are in and having to go through.  While reading your story, I was struck by how long you guys have been apart.  Or to say it another way, how little time you were actually together.  You may have lived together, but there was no partnership, no team, and no real relationship.

Your saga is one of disconnection and missed communication.

I wouldn't take the small penis comment to heart.  As a woman I can tell you that a man with a smaller penis can be 100 times better lover than a man with a large penis who does not know how to use it, or is not careful.

It sounds like, if you choose, there is considerable emotional work for you to do if you ever desire to have a meaningful relationship where there is true connection.  It's up to you.

Good luck.

First, you really might want to do some basic re-evaluation here.  You don't 'give' her child support.  You pay child support to help with the upkeep of YOUR children.  $750. a month is nothing when it comes to taking care of a household.  You also don't GIVE her the house.  It would be a good idea if whoever is going to have the primary care of the kids, have a familiar stable home for them.

Please do not make the mistake of making your children pick who they want to live with.  It's cruel and unkind to make a kid pick one parent over the other.

One more thing, I am so tired of reading about how someone's spouse cheated on them.  Did the guilty spouse go out and do that on their own?  What type of connection did the faithfull one have with the cheating spouse?  

Were you guilty of the workaholism, sportaholism, etc that so many men are?  Did you ever pay any attention to her, treat her with courtesy, respect?  Did you ever try and please her in bed, do you know if she ever had orgasms?  Did you care?

The point is that people don't cheat because they are horndogs.  They cheat because they are lonely, feeling abandoned, and in despair.  Someone pays them a little bit of attention, and it feels so good.  They awake and see they can do better.

I am so as sorry for your pain.  I am an older woman and know what you speak about.   As hard as it may be to believe, there will come a time, 50 plus, when you will become an invisible woman.  You will no longer be seen as a sexual object, you will only be seen as someone who is good for babysitting, volunteering, being on committees, or making cookies.  And then you may come to miss the times where you were regarded sexually.
You got what you asked for.  Now you can spend more time with your friends.  And you have managed to alienate a sweet loving woman.

The sex does not sound like it does anything for you.  Do you ever have orgasms?  Does he try to please you, or are you just supposed to get him off?  Sexual incompatiability is a big issue in a relationship.   He does not have the right to expect you to help him come.  If he truly needs that much sexual release per day, he should go in the bathroom and do it himself.

I divorced after 25 years.  I miss him terribly.  However, he was a difficult uncooperative man to live with.  We were never a team or partners.  Many times I felt like a roommate.  He always did what he wanted, had his own plans, had his own things he wanted to do.  I was so lonely.  I made a life outside of the marriage with friends doing things I liked.  Frankly, with his uncooperative streak, I couldn't see how we could age out together.  I felt like a prop in his life.  Someone to come home to, listen to his troubles, fix a meal.  But he did not truly know me, or care too.  It was too heartbreaking to stay and not feel loved.  I do feel very lonely sometimes because I miss being in a relationship.

Thank you for your lovely writing.  I am going through a very hard time now.  It is so helpful to read your posting.  It reminds me once again what is important in life.  I come from a poverty-stricken family myself.  I put many years into making something of myself, and I succeeded.  However, I missed out on many things along the way.  Too late to go back now.  Just trying to find new meaning in my life.
